intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect baggage and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park (note: hotel is in Buena Park, CA — confirm Hawaii hotel booking separately). After settling in, take a leisurely stroll to the nearest beach to get your first feel of Hawaii. If staying on Oahu, head to Waikiki Beach for a relaxed first afternoon — swim, sunbathe, and soak in the atmosphere. Entrance is free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Waikiki strip on foot. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free nightly shows around sunset). Pick up groceries or snacks at a nearby ABC Store or Foodland for budget-friendly supplies.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival — try Starbucks or a local airport café (~$8–10).
meals.lunch: Pick up a plate lunch from a local food truck near Waikiki — look for Hawaiian BBQ or poke bowls (~$10–14).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Marugame Udon in Waikiki — hearty udon noodles starting at $8. Family-friendly and very budget-conscious.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow for travel fatigue and settling in. Keep receipts and set a daily spending target of ~$60–80 per adult to stay on budget throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — start early (arrive by 6:00–7:00 AM to beat crowds and heat). This manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater rewards hikers with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Admission is $5 per person (or $10 per car). Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, cool off at Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) — a quieter, family-friendly alternative to busy Waikiki. Snorkeling is excellent here with calm, clear water. Bring or rent snorkel gear (~$10–15 rental nearby).
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Waikiki. Visit the free Honolulu Zoo grounds area or walk through Kapiolani Park. Enjoy the open green space with the kids before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack granola bars and fruit from the grocery store the night before — eat before the hike to save money (~$3–5).
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Diamond Head — a legendary local spot. Plate lunches with rice and macaroni salad from ~$10–13.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — a beloved local poke shop. Build-your-own poke bowls from ~$12–15. Cash preferred, arrive early as lines form quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head State Monument opens at 6:00 AM. Reservations are required in advance at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. August weather averages 16–28°C so mornings are ideal for hiking. Carry rain gear as brief showers are common.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's top snorkeling spots and a protected marine sanctuary. Arrive early (opens 6:45 AM) as entry is capped daily. Admission is $25 per adult, free for children under 12. A short educational video is required before entering the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Kalanianaole Highway along the southeastern coast. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free) and Sandy Beach Park — a beautiful but rough-surf beach great for watching bodyboarders. Families should stay on the sand here as currents are strong.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area. Let the kids enjoy the beach at sunset. Browse the International Market Place outdoor mall — free to walk through with street performers and local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel if a kitchenette is available — instant oatmeal, fruit, and juice (~$4–6). Alternatively, grab a malasada (Portuguese donut) from Leonard's Bakery on the way (~$1.50 each).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Sandy Beach — sandwiches, chips, and drinks from Foodland (~$8–10 per person).
meals.dinner: Zippy's Restaurant — a Hawaii institution with affordable local comfort food. Chili, saimin noodles, and plate lunches from ~$9–13. Family-friendly atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online (hanauma bay.hawaii.gov). Slots fill up weeks in advance in August — book before your trip. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only, as chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the coral.

day_by_day.morning: Explore downtown Honolulu — visit Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on US soil). Guided tours start at $27 for adults, $7 for children. Alternatively, the grounds are free to walk. Nearby, visit the King Kamehameha Statue and Hawaii State Capitol (free exterior viewing).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Chinatown Honolulu — a vibrant, historic neighborhood with colorful murals, local markets, and lei shops. Browse the Oahu Market and pick up fresh tropical fruits cheaply. Visit the Foster Botanical Garden (~$5 admission) — a peaceful urban garden with massive ancient trees, great for families.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free Friday Night Art Walk if timing aligns, or simply enjoy a sunset walk along Ala Moana Beach Park — a long, calm beach popular with locals and perfect for families. Free parking and facilities available.

meals.breakfast: Visit Liliha Bakery — a Honolulu classic open early. Try their famous cocoa puffs and breakfast plates from ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Eat at Chinatown's Maunakea Marketplace food court — authentic Asian-Hawaiian dishes from multiple vendors for ~$7–10 per person.
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Food Court at Ala Moana Center — huge variety of local and Asian food stalls. Budget meals from ~$8–12. Great for families with picky eaters.

day_by_day.notes: Chinatown is best explored on foot. Keep an eye on belongings in busy market areas. Foster Botanical Garden is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — highly recommended for families with curious kids.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore of Oahu (about 1 hour from Waikiki). Stop at Waimea Valley — a beautiful botanical garden and cultural park with a stunning waterfall and swimming hole. Admission is $20 adults, $10 children. The 0.75-mile walk to the falls is easy and family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline). In August, summer swells mean calm, swimmable water — perfect for families. Walk the shoreline, collect shells, and enjoy the laid-back North Shore vibe. All beaches are free.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Haleiwa Town on the way back — the charming surf town of the North Shore. Browse local shops and art galleries. Don't miss Matsumoto Shave Ice — a legendary Hawaii treat (~$4–6).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel or pack snacks for the drive — fruit, granola bars, and water (~$3–5).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa or Kahuku — famous garlic shrimp plates for ~$14–16. A North Shore institution worth every penny.
meals.dinner: Kono's Restaurant in Haleiwa — casual, affordable burritos and local-style wraps from ~$10–13. Eat on the outdoor patio.

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for this day is highly recommended (~$40–60/day from budget rental companies). North Shore is about 35 miles from Waikiki. August is the best time to visit as summer surf is calm and safe for swimming. Bring cash for shrimp trucks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free (timed entry passes required — reserve at recreation.gov). The visitor center and exhibits are also free. Plan 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, head to Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — if not open today, substitute with a visit to Pearlridge Center or a nearby beach). Alternatively, visit the Bishop Museum (~$25 adults, $17 children) — Hawaii's premier natural history and cultural museum, excellent for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for the free Kuhio Beach Torch Lighting and Hula Show — held nightly at sunset. A wonderful, authentic cultural experience at no cost. Great photo opportunity for families.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at McDonald's / Jamba Juice near Waikiki (~$6–9) — keep it light before the Pearl Harbor visit.
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor has a café on-site (moderate pricing ~$12–15) or pack your own lunch to eat at the picnic areas outside the memorial.
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki — a beloved local breakfast-all-day diner. Pancakes, waffles, and omelets from ~$12–16. Fun for families and very filling.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed-entry passes for the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour book up months in advance — reserve online before your trip. The memorial is free but the boat tour requires a reservation. Dress respectfully (no swimwear). Allow extra time for security screening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (open Saturdays 7:30 AM – 11:00 AM) — one of Oahu's best farmers markets with local produce, prepared foods, fresh juices, and handmade crafts. Free to browse, great for picking up affordable local snacks and gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Lanikai Beach on the Windward Coast (about 30 minutes from Waikiki) — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. Calm, turquoise water ideal for families. Free access. Kayak rentals to the Mokulua Islands available nearby (~$30–40/hour for a double kayak).
day_by_day.evening: Drive through Kailua Town — a charming, walkable beach town with boutique shops and local restaurants. Browse without pressure to buy and enjoy the relaxed local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the KCC Farmers Market — fresh açaí bowls, malasadas, local fruit, and coffee from various vendors (~$8–12).
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — a beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches, salads, and poke from ~$10–14.
meals.dinner: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for creative pancakes and local comfort food. Dinner plates from ~$13–18. Family-friendly with generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has limited parking — arrive early or park in Kailua and walk/bike the 1.5 miles. Bike rentals are available in Kailua (~$15–20/day) and are a fun family activity. The Pillbox Hike above Lanikai offers stunning views but is moderately challenging — optional for older kids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii on the Windward Coast (~$40 adults, $20 children) — a family-favorite marine park with dolphin shows, penguin encounters, sea turtle exhibits, and a Hawaiian reef tank. Budget-friendly compared to mainland theme parks and highly engaging for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Sea Life Park, stop at Makapuu Beach Park — a scenic beach with a dramatic backdrop of sea cliffs. The water can be rough, but the beach and views are stunning. Walk the Makapuu Lighthouse Trail (free, 2-mile round trip, paved) for sweeping coastal views. Easy enough for families.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Spend the evening at Duke's Waikiki for a beachfront sunset — you don't need to dine there to enjoy the view. Walk the Waikiki Beach Walk promenade and let the kids play in the sand one more time.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple hotel breakfast — cereal, fruit, and juice purchased from the grocery store (~$4–6).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Makapuu Beach — sandwiches, chips, and cold drinks from a nearby convenience store (~$8–10 per person).
meals.dinner: Wailana Coffee House in Waikiki — a 24-hour local diner with affordable Hawaiian and American comfort food. Plates from ~$10–15. Very family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park tickets are cheaper when purchased online in advance. Check their website for family bundle deals. The Makapuu Lighthouse Trail is stroller-accessible and offers whale-watching opportunities (though August is not peak whale season). Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of the University of Hawaii at Manoa campus — beautiful tropical grounds with free art installations and the East-West Center gardens. Nearby, visit Manoa Falls Trail (free parking ~$5, trail is free) — a lush, 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a rainforest to a 150-foot waterfall. Muddy but magical, especially after rain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ala Moana Beach Park — Honolulu's largest beach park with calm, protected water ideal for families. Rent a paddleboard or kayak (~$15–20/hour) or simply relax on the wide sandy beach. The park has excellent facilities including showers, restrooms, and picnic areas — all free.
day_by_day.evening: Final shopping and souvenir hunting at Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air mall. Look for affordable local gifts at Longs Drugs, ABC Stores, or the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet style vendors. Enjoy a final sunset walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Visit Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — known for creative breakfast dishes and açaí bowls from ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Poke to the Max near Ala Moana — build-your-own poke bowls with generous portions from ~$12–15. One of the best value poke spots on the island.
meals.dinner: Side Street Inn — a beloved local hangout with large, shareable plates of local comfort food. Fried rice, pork chops, and calamari from ~$12–18 per dish. Perfect for a family-style final dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Manoa Falls Trail can be very muddy — wear closed-toe shoes or water sandals. The trail passes through a mosquito-heavy rainforest so bring insect repellent. This is one of the most beautiful and accessible hikes on Oahu, especially after light rain when the falls are at full flow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — wake up early for one last sunrise on Waikiki Beach. Take a slow walk along the shoreline, collect a few shells, and soak in the last moments of paradise. If time allows, grab a final shave ice or malasada from a nearby vendor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and head to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and boarding. Return any rental car if applicable.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the aloha spirit home. Review your trip budget and celebrate a successful, affordable Hawaii adventure.

meals.breakfast: One last plate lunch or breakfast at a local spot near the hotel — try Loco Moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, and gravy) at a local diner for ~$10–12. A quintessential Hawaii farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Airport dining at HNL — Makai Market Food Court in the terminal offers local options including poke, saimin, and plate lunches from ~$12–16.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or snacks purchased before boarding — pack leftover snacks from the trip to save money on airport food.

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car at least 3 hours before departure to allow for shuttle time and check-in. Double-check all hotel rooms and beach bags for forgotten items. Consider purchasing a reusable tote bag with local art as a budget-friendly souvenir (~$5–10 at ABC Stores). Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

This is an ideal indoor midday or rainy-day activity for families, offering hours of educational entertainment while staying cool and sheltered.

experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Honolulu International Airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer. Check in early if possible at your Oahu accommodation (note: your booking shows a Buena Park, CA address — confirm Hawaii lodging separately). Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (about 20 minutes from the airport) for a relaxed first afternoon. Stroll the beachfront, dip your toes in the warm Pacific, and let the kids enjoy the gentle waves. Pick up a local SIM card or grab snacks at an ABC Store along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual welcome dinner at Duke's Waikiki on the beach — a beloved local institution with open-air seating, fresh fish tacos, hula pie dessert, and live Hawaiian music. Perfect for families and mid-range budgets (~$20–35 per adult).

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival — Island Brew Coffeehouse in the terminal is a solid option.
meals.lunch: Pick up plate lunches from a nearby food truck or Rainbow Drive-In near Kapahulu Ave — a classic local spot with loco moco and mixed plates (~$10–14 per person).
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki (2335 Kalakaua Ave) — fresh seafood, burgers, and Hawaiian classics with ocean views. Budget ~$25–35 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the late-morning arrival. Prioritize rest and acclimatization. August in Hawaii averages highs around 85°F (29°C) — sunscreen and hydration are essential from day one. Confirm your actual Hawaii hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit. Depart by 6:30 AM to beat the heat and crowds. The 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside the volcanic crater takes about 1.5–2 hours and rewards you with sweeping panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific. Suitable for older kids (ages 6+). Entry fee is $5/person; book timed entry online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, head to Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) — a quieter, family-friendly alternative to busy Waikiki. Calm, clear water ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Rent snorkel gear nearby (~$15/set) and explore the reef. Relax on the sand through the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or drive to Kapahulu Avenue for dinner at Ono Seafood — a no-frills, beloved poke shop. Then stroll to Leonard's Bakery for fresh malasadas (Portuguese donuts) — a Hawaii must-do for families.

meals.breakfast: Grab acai bowls or smoothies at Bogart's Cafe near Diamond Head before the hike (~$10–14 per person).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Kaimana Beach — pick up bento boxes or musubi from Lawson's or a nearby convenience store (~$8–12 per person).
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood (747 Kapahulu Ave) for fresh poke bowls (~$12–18 per person), followed by malasadas at Leonard's Bakery (~$2–4 each).

day_by_day.notes: Book Diamond Head timed entry at gostateparks.hawaii.gov well in advance — slots fill up fast, especially in August. Wear closed-toe shoes for the hike and bring water. The hike involves stairs and a tunnel — manageable for most families.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for a world-class snorkeling experience. Arrive early (gates open at 6:45 AM) — the bay reaches capacity quickly and closes to new visitors by mid-morning. Watch the mandatory 9-minute marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in the protected bay. Entry is $25/adult, free for children under 12.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Makapuu Coastal Trail (30 minutes east) — a paved, stroller-accessible 2-mile round-trip walk with stunning ocean views and whale-watching potential. Then stop at Makapuu Beach for a rest and photos of the dramatic coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Waikiki and enjoy dinner at Marukame Udon in the heart of Waikiki — a wildly popular, affordable Japanese udon restaurant with a cafeteria-style line. Expect a short wait but excellent value.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua (~$12–18 per person) — famous for red velvet pancakes and local-style eggs Benedict. A short detour but worth it.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or grab shave ice and snacks at the Hanauma Bay snack bar (~$8–12 per person) after snorkeling.
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon (2310 Kuhio Ave, Waikiki) — fresh udon noodles, tempura, and onigiri. Budget-friendly at ~$8–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations made online at huihanaumabay.com — reservations open 2 days in advance at 7:00 AM HST and sell out immediately. Do not miss this booking window. Reef-safe sunscreen only is permitted inside the bay.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Oahu's North Shore (about 1 hour from Waikiki) for the Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town. Explore the charming surf village at your own pace — browse local boutiques, visit Matsumoto Shave Ice (a legendary institution since 1951), and soak in the laid-back North Shore vibe. August is summer, so waves are calm and perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Bay Beach Park — one of Hawaii's most iconic beaches. In summer, the bay is calm and ideal for swimming, cliff jumping (for adventurous older kids/adults), and snorkeling. Spend 2–3 hours here. Nearby, visit Waimea Valley for a short nature walk to a beautiful waterfall (~$20/adult, $10/child).
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa before heading back — a beloved local spot known for massive burritos, kalua pork, and fresh ingredients. Then make the scenic drive back to your hotel along the Kamehameha Highway.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and pastries at Haleiwa Coffee Gallery or Café Haleiwa upon arrival on the North Shore (~$8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice for dessert (~$4–7), plus a plate lunch from Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (cash only, ~$14–16 per plate) — a North Shore legend.
meals.dinner: Kono's Northshore (66-250 Kamehameha Hwy, Haleiwa) — hearty burritos and local flavors, ~$12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore drive is beautiful but can take longer than expected with traffic. Leave Waikiki by 8:30 AM to make the most of the day. Giovanni's Shrimp Truck is cash only — bring small bills. August surf on the North Shore is gentle and family-safe.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie on Oahu's North Shore (about 1 hour from Waikiki). Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village exhibits — Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Hawaii, Marquesas, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. Ideal for families with children of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon (typically around 2:30 PM), a spectacular free-flowing cultural parade. Explore the IMAX theater and gift shops. The center is large enough to fill a full day.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking Polynesian song and dance spectacular with fire knife dancing and stunning costumes. Combine with the Ali'i Luau dinner package for an authentic luau feast (poi, kalua pig, haupia dessert). Book the combo package in advance (~$120–160/adult, ~$80–100/child).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a quick meal at McDonald's or Jamba Juice near Waikiki before departing (~$8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Dining options inside the Polynesian Cultural Center — the Gateway Restaurant offers a buffet with Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (~$18–25 per person, included in some packages).
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an all-inclusive luau feast with traditional Hawaiian foods, entertainment, and the Ha show. Pre-book online at polynesia.com.

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is closed on Sundays. Book tickets well in advance at polynesia.com — the luau and evening show packages sell out weeks ahead in August. Plan to spend 6–8 hours here. Parking is free on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight from Honolulu to Maui (Kahului Airport) — flights run frequently and take about 30 minutes (~$60–100/person each way on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest). Pick up a rental car at Kahului Airport and drive to the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Maalaea (about 15 minutes from the airport).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend 2–3 hours at the Maui Ocean Center — Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a stunning walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, hammerhead sharks, manta rays, and interactive exhibits. Excellent for families. Entry is ~$35/adult, ~$25/child. Afterward, drive to Kaanapali Beach (about 45 minutes) — one of Maui's most beautiful stretches of sand — for a relaxing late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset at Kaanapali Beach and watch the famous cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a free nightly tradition where a torch-lighter dives from the lava rock at sunset. Dine at Hula Grill Kaanapali on the beach for fresh fish and Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near your Oahu hotel before the airport transfer — Liliha Bakery is a local favorite for coco puffs and saimin (~$10–15 per person).
meals.lunch: Maui Ocean Center has a café on-site, or grab fish tacos at Maalaea Grill nearby (~$12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Kaanapali (2435 Kaanapali Pkwy) — open-air beachfront dining with fresh catch, burgers, and tropical cocktails. Budget ~$25–40 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2–3 weeks in advance for best prices. Confirm your Maui accommodation separately. August is peak season on Maui — book all restaurants and activities ahead. The cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock happens nightly around sunset (approximately 7:00–7:30 PM in August).

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the legendary Road to Hana drive — one of the world's most scenic coastal roads. Depart by 7:00 AM from Kaanapali (about 1.5 hours to the start of the road in Paia). Stop at Twin Falls (easy family hike to waterfalls), the Garden of Eden Arboretum (~$20/car), and Waikamoi Nature Trail. Pick up fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's in Keanae — a Road to Hana institution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Wailua Falls overlook, Waianapanapa State Park (black sand beach — requires advance reservation at gostateparks.hawaii.gov, ~$5/person), and the town of Hana itself. Explore Hamoa Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful and secluded beaches — for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive back toward Kaanapali (allow 2.5–3 hours). Stop for dinner in Paia Town — a charming hippie surf town with excellent restaurants. Flatbread Company in Paia is a family favorite with wood-fired pizzas and local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee at Paia Bay Coffee & Bar in Paia before starting the Hana drive (~$8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Roadside stops along the Hana Highway — fresh fruit stands, coconut water, and Aunty Sandy's banana bread (~$10–15 total). Pack a cooler with snacks and drinks.
meals.dinner: Flatbread Company (89 Hana Hwy, Paia) — organic wood-fired pizzas, salads, and local craft beers. Budget ~$18–28 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment — 620+ curves and 59 bridges over 52 miles. Start early to avoid traffic. Waianapanapa State Park reservations are mandatory and must be booked at gostateparks.hawaii.gov. Bring motion sickness remedies for young children. Gas up before leaving Paia — there are very few stations along the route.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at Kaanapali Beach — one of Maui's finest. Rent snorkel gear (~$15/set) and snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), which is teeming with sea turtles, reef fish, and vibrant coral. This is one of Maui's best shore snorkeling spots and is very family-friendly with calm, clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Lahaina Town (10 minutes south of Kaanapali) for an afternoon of exploration. Visit the historic Banyan Tree — the largest in the US, planted in 1873 — and browse the Front Street galleries, shops, and art scene. Note: Lahaina is in recovery following the 2023 wildfires; check current access and support local businesses. Visit the Lahaina Heritage Museum for context.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner cruise from Lahaina Harbor — a popular family activity offering views of Maui's coastline, potential dolphin sightings, and a buffet dinner. Pacific Whale Foundation offers eco-friendly options (~$80–110/adult, ~$50–70/child). Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Gazebo Restaurant in Napili (arrive early — long waits but worth it for macadamia nut pancakes and ocean views, ~$12–18 per person).
meals.lunch: Grab shave ice and plate lunches in Lahaina — Ululani's Hawaiian Shave Ice is a Maui favorite (~$5–8 per shave ice). Lunch at Aloha Mixed Plate on the waterfront (~$14–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner cruise from Lahaina Harbor — buffet dinner with Hawaiian and American fare included in the cruise package. Book through Pacific Whale Foundation or Trilogy Excursions.

day_by_day.notes: Lahaina is slowly rebuilding after the devastating August 2023 wildfires. Visiting and spending money at local businesses is a meaningful way to support the community. Check current conditions and access restrictions before visiting. The sunset cruise is a highlight for families — book well in advance for August.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided kayak and snorkel tour along Maui's south coast from Makena or Kihei (~$65–85/adult, ~$45–60/child). Paddle to sea caves, lava arches, and pristine snorkeling spots teeming with Hawaiian green sea turtles. Many operators offer family-friendly tours with tandem kayaks for younger children. South Maui Guides and Makena Kayak Tours are reputable options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Makena State Park (Big Beach) — one of Maui's most spectacular beaches with a wide, golden sand shore and dramatic backdrop. Swim in the clear turquoise water (note: shore break can be powerful — supervise children closely). Walk over the lava rock to Little Beach for a quieter, more secluded spot.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Kihei for a casual, affordable dinner — Kihei Caffe is a local institution for comfort food. Then enjoy a final Maui evening stroll along the Kihei coastline and pick up souvenirs at the Kihei Kalama Village market.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Kihei Caffe (1945 S Kihei Rd) — a beloved local diner with massive portions and low prices (~$10–15 per person). Arrive early as lines form quickly.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Big Beach — grab sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from Foodland Farms in Kihei (~$10–15 per person) before heading to Makena.
meals.dinner: Da Kitchen in Kihei — a local favorite for generous Hawaiian plate lunches, loco moco, and fresh fish. Budget-friendly at ~$14–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Big Beach (Oneloa Beach) at Makena State Park has no lifeguards — the shore break can be deceptively powerful even on calm days. Supervise children carefully and avoid the water if waves are large. The kayak tour should be booked 1–2 weeks in advance. Wear reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at your Maui beach. Pack up and check out of your accommodation. Drive to Kahului for a final stop at the Maui Swap Meet at the University of Hawaii Maui College (open Saturday mornings — if timing aligns) or browse the shops at Queen Ka'ahumanu Center for last-minute souvenirs and local goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kahului Airport for your return inter-island flight to Honolulu, then connect to your mainland flight home. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for inter-island connections and security. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Oahu and Maui.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or airport dining — grab a final plate lunch or poke bowl at Kahului Airport's local food options before departure. Pick up Hawaiian Host macadamia chocolates and Kona coffee as gifts at the airport shops.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast at Nalu's South Shore Grill in Kihei or your hotel restaurant — enjoy one last acai bowl or loco moco (~$12–18 per person).
meals.lunch: Poke bowl or plate lunch at Kahului Airport — Maui Tacos or local vendors in the terminal (~$12–16 per person).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dining at Honolulu Airport during your connection — Makai Market Food Court in the main terminal has local options (~$12–18 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for inter-island connections — Hawaiian Airlines recommends arriving 90 minutes before inter-island flights, but 2+ hours is safer during peak August travel. Confirm all return flight details the night before. Mahalo for an amazing Hawaii adventure — a hui hou (until we meet again)!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
experiences.description: A family-friendly snorkeling adventure in a protected marine sanctuary teeming with colorful fish and sea turtles. Arrive early to secure entry and enjoy calm, clear waters before crowds build. An indoor education center provides a great rainy-day or midday alternative with marine life exhibits.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience
experiences.description: An immersive family cultural experience featuring six Polynesian villages, live performances, canoe rides, and traditional craft demonstrations. The indoor evening luau and IMAX theater make it a perfect option to avoid midday heat while learning about Hawaiian and Pacific Island heritage.

experiences.name: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit
experiences.description: A manageable 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside a volcanic crater offering panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. Best tackled at sunrise to beat the heat and crowds. Kids ages 5 and up can typically complete this trail, making it a memorable family achievement.

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit
experiences.description: Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring a walk-through underwater tunnel, Hawaiian green sea turtles, manta rays, and interactive tide pools. This is an ideal indoor midday or rainy-day activity for families, offering hours of educational entertainment while staying cool and sheltered.

experiences.name: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town
experiences.description: Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore with a self-guided food tour sampling legendary shave ice at Matsumoto's, fresh poke bowls, garlic shrimp from roadside trucks, and tropical fruit smoothies. Best enjoyed in the cooler morning or early evening hours while browsing local shops and galleries.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beach or hotel pool area to decompress from travel. Visit a nearby luxury shopping center or resort promenade to pick up any essentials and get oriented with the local surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a premium oceanfront restaurant near the hotel. Enjoy fresh Hawaiian seafood and local cuisine to kick off the trip in style. Toast to the beginning of your Hawaii adventure.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight before landing
meals.lunch: Room service or hotel restaurant upon check-in — try a fresh poke bowl or Hawaiian plate lunch
meals.dinner: Roy's Hawaii Kai or a comparable upscale Hawaiian fusion restaurant — signature misoyaki butterfish and fresh island cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, keep Day 1 relaxed. No major excursions scheduled — focus on arrival, check-in, and gentle acclimatization. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and private transfers for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — Arrive early (7:30–8:00 AM) to beat crowds at this protected marine sanctuary. Enjoy a family-friendly snorkeling adventure surrounded by colorful tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs in crystal-clear waters. Reserve premium snorkel gear rentals in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the scenic Koko Head area for a relaxed beachside lunch, then explore the nearby Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach Park for stunning coastal views and photo opportunities. Keep younger family members safely back from the blowhole.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area for a relaxed evening. Enjoy sunset views from a rooftop bar or beachside lounge before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or grab-and-go acai bowls from a local café before heading to Hanauma Bay
meals.lunch: Koko Marina Center — try Zippy's or a local plate lunch spot for an authentic Hawaiian midday meal
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia Waikiki — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's upscale Asian-Hawaiian fusion restaurant with stunning ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and charges an entry fee. Arrive before 8 AM to secure parking. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are prohibited to protect the marine ecosystem. August weather averages around 16–17°C in the morning, so bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Hike to Diamond Head Summit — Depart hotel by 5:30 AM for the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip hike inside the volcanic crater. Reach the summit at sunrise for breathtaking panoramic views of Waikiki, the Pacific Ocean, and Honolulu skyline. The manageable trail is suitable for older children and families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a premium beach afternoon. Arrange private surf lessons or outrigger canoe rides through the hotel concierge. Relax on a reserved beach cabana with butler service at a luxury Waikiki resort beach club.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Waikiki's upscale dining and entertainment scene. Catch a traditional Hawaiian hula performance at a beachfront venue before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-hike snack — granola bars and fruit; post-hike brunch at Eggs 'n Things Waikiki for famous pancakes and local favorites
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and tropical cocktails right on the sand
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel — Honolulu's most celebrated fine dining restaurant with French-Hawaiian cuisine and impeccable ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head State Monument opens at 6:00 AM. Book tickets online in advance as capacity is limited. Bring water, sunscreen, and comfortable hiking shoes. The hike involves some steep stairs and a tunnel — manageable for most ages but not recommended for toddlers or those with mobility issues.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Experience — Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. A world-class family experience on Oahu's North Shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center with the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular floating parade of Polynesian cultures. Explore the IMAX theater and interactive exhibits. The center is a full-day experience worth savoring.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous HA: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production featuring over 100 performers, fire dancing, and traditional music. Enjoy the premium Ali'i Luau dinner package with reserved seating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for the North Shore — full American or Hawaiian breakfast at the hotel restaurant
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with premium package, featuring Hawaiian, Polynesian, and American cuisine
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — premium luau dinner with kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and tropical beverages included in the evening show package

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center's Ambassador Package well in advance — it includes priority access, guided tours, reserved luau seating, and the evening show. The drive from the hotel area to Laie on the North Shore takes approximately 45–60 minutes. Arrange a private driver or luxury shuttle for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Shave Ice and Local Food Tour in Haleiwa Town — Explore the charming surf town of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore. Start with the legendary Matsumoto Shave Ice, then wander through local boutiques, art galleries, and surf shops. Sample fresh tropical fruits, malasadas (Portuguese donuts), and local snacks along the main street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Bay Beach Park for a stunning North Shore beach afternoon. Swim in the calm summer waters (August is ideal — winter swells are absent), explore the rocky shoreline, and enjoy the lush tropical scenery. Alternatively, visit Waimea Valley for a guided botanical garden walk and cliff jumping at the waterfall (family-friendly).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area via scenic coastal route. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset cocktail cruise or beachside bonfire experience arranged through the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore in Haleiwa — famous breakfast burritos and local morning plates in a casual surf-town atmosphere
meals.lunch: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — waterfront dining with fresh catch of the day, coconut shrimp, and tropical salads overlooking the Anahulu River
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — celebrity chef Nobu Matsuhisa's signature Japanese-Peruvian fusion with premium omakase options and fresh Hawaiian ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Haleiwa is approximately 45 minutes from the hotel. August is the best time to visit the North Shore as the ocean is calm and perfect for swimming. Waimea Valley charges a separate entry fee — book in advance. The shave ice experience is a quintessential Hawaii must-do for families.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui — Arrange an early morning flight from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului (OGG) on Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines. Flight duration is approximately 35–40 minutes. Transfer to Maui accommodations via private luxury car service. Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium Visit — Hawaii's premier aquarium in Maalaea Harbor. Explore the walk-through underwater tunnel surrounded by sharks, rays, and tropical fish. Meet Hawaiian green sea turtles, watch live jellyfish exhibits, and enjoy the open-ocean tank. Highly engaging for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lahaina Town for a classic Maui evening. Stroll the historic waterfront, browse art galleries, and watch the sunset over the Pacific from the famous Banyan Tree Park.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or airport lounge breakfast before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Seascape Maalaea Restaurant at Maui Ocean Center — fresh seafood with harbor views, right at the aquarium
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill — one of Maui's most acclaimed fine dining restaurants with New American cuisine, fresh island fish, and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Hawaiian Airlines offers the most reliable service between Oahu and Maui. The Maui Ocean Center is open daily and tickets can be purchased online. Lahaina is approximately 20 minutes from Maalaea — arrange a private driver for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — Embark on the legendary scenic drive along Maui's northeastern coastline. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the Ke'anae Peninsula overlook, and visit the Garden of Eden Arboretum. The lush rainforest scenery, dramatic sea cliffs, and cascading waterfalls make this one of Hawaii's most iconic experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Wailua Falls and the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park. Explore the lava sea caves and dramatic coastal scenery. Arrive in Hana Town for a relaxing afternoon break.
day_by_day.evening: Return along the Road to Hana (or complete the loop via Upcountry Maui if time permits). Enjoy a quiet, luxurious evening at your Maui resort with in-room dining or a spa treatment.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing — the Road to Hana is best started by 7:00–8:00 AM
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's, coconut candy, and tropical fruit from local vendors
meals.dinner: In-room private dining at your Maui luxury resort, or Mama's Fish House in Paia — one of Hawaii's most celebrated seafood restaurants with fresh catch sourced daily from local fishermen

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles with over 600 curves and 59 bridges — allow a full day. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations for parking. Bring motion sickness remedies for younger children. August rain (176mm monthly average) may affect some stops — have a flexible plan. A private guided tour is recommended for a stress-free experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakala Crater — Wake before dawn for the drive up to Haleakala National Park summit (10,023 feet). Watch the spectacular sunrise above the clouds from the summit of this dormant volcano — a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience. Dress warmly as summit temperatures can drop to near freezing even in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and explore Upcountry Maui — visit Surfing Goat Dairy for a family-friendly farm tour and cheese tasting, browse the Makawao town boutiques, and stop at the Lavender Farm at Ali'i Kula for stunning views and artisan products.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Wailea Beach for a premium sunset beach experience. Enjoy cocktails at a luxury resort beach bar as the sun sets over the Pacific and neighboring islands of Lanai and Kahoolawe come into silhouette.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed gourmet breakfast box from the hotel to enjoy at the Haleakala summit — coffee, pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Upcountry Maui — Casanova Italian Restaurant in Makawao for wood-fired pizza and fresh pasta in a charming cowboy-town setting
meals.dinner: Spago Maui at Four Seasons Resort Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's signature California-Hawaiian cuisine with panoramic ocean views and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked online through recreation.gov up to 60 days in advance — this is non-negotiable. Depart hotel by 3:00–3:30 AM for the summit. Bring heavy layers — summit temperatures average 4–10°C even in summer. The experience is absolutely worth the early wake-up.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury Snorkel and Whale Watch Catamaran Cruise — Board a premium private or small-group catamaran from Maalaea Harbor or Lahaina Harbor. Sail to Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic caldera with exceptional visibility (up to 150 feet) and abundant marine life. Snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish species in this protected marine sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the catamaran cruise to Turtle Town near Makena for more snorkeling with Hawaiian green sea turtles. Enjoy onboard gourmet lunch, open bar, and premium snorkel equipment. Return to harbor by mid-afternoon. Spend the remaining afternoon relaxing at Wailea Beach or the resort pool.
day_by_day.evening: Final Maui evening — indulge in a luxury spa treatment at your resort (couples massage or family spa package), followed by a memorable farewell dinner at one of Maui's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full buffet or à la carte at the hotel restaurant overlooking the ocean
meals.lunch: Gourmet onboard lunch on the catamaran — fresh deli sandwiches, tropical fruit, salads, and open bar with tropical cocktails and non-alcoholic options
meals.dinner: Humble Market Kitchin at Wailea Beach Resort — Chef Roy Yamaguchi's farm-to-table Hawaiian regional cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini catamaran cruise through a premium operator such as Trilogy Excursions or Pride of Maui — reserve well in advance as spots fill quickly in August. The cruise typically runs 7:00 AM–1:00 PM. August conditions are generally calm and ideal for snorkeling. Children of all ages are welcome.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Maui — Enjoy a leisurely luxury resort breakfast and take one last swim at Wailea Beach or the resort pool. Pack up and check out. Arrange a private car transfer to Kahului Airport (OGG) for the inter-island flight back to Honolulu, then connect to your mainland departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, stop at the Shops at Wailea for last-minute luxury shopping — pick up premium Hawaiian gifts, macadamia nut products, Kona coffee, and local artisan souvenirs. Alternatively, enjoy a final shave ice or malasada at a local favorite near the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with incredible memories. If the return flight is late evening, enjoy a final dinner at Honolulu Airport's premium dining options or arrange a layover dinner in Waikiki before the mainland flight.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — splurge on the full luxury buffet with fresh tropical fruits, eggs benedict, loco moco, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman in Wailea — farm-to-table casual fine dining with fresh local ingredients, craft cocktails, and live Hawaiian music
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final Waikiki dinner if layover permits — consider Orchids at Halekulani for a refined farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the inter-island connection and security. Maui's Kahului Airport can be busy on Monday mornings. Confirm all luggage weight limits — premium Hawaiian souvenirs and gifts can add up quickly. Consider shipping larger items home via FedEx or UPS from the resort concierge to avoid baggage fees.
